resources.string: This translation has not been reviewed by a native speaker.
foxhg edits Pokémon HeartGold and SoulSilver (English, .nds). A project keeps your changes in a folder and saves them as you work. Your ROM is never modified: Build ROM writes a new file.
Pick an editor on the left. Changes are saved into the project automatically.
Pick an editor on the left. Without a project, changes stay in memory until you save them as a project or choose Build ROM….
A project keeps your changes in a folder and saves them automatically. The ROM is never modified or copied.
Choose where to create the project
Choose the ROM this project edits
Choose a folder that does not exist yet or is empty
You edited a ROM without a project, so these changes exist only in memory. Save them as a project to keep them, or discard them. You can also cancel and use Build ROM… to write a patched ROM.
The save file is not written
You edited %1$s but did not write it. Write it (the file that is there is kept as .bak), or discard the changes.
If you moved or renamed it, point the project at it again. Your saved changes are kept.
Where the ROM goes is {rom}; without it the ROM is added at the end. For example: desmume {rom} or retroarch -L /path/to/desmume_libretro.so {rom}

Writes a save that continues at the place you pick, with an empty party, bag and PC, to start the game anywhere (for example in a Poké Mart you edited). The map and tile must exist and be walkable. To play from the beginning, start a new game in the game itself.
A name has at most %1$d characters
Effort points given when this Pokémon is defeated (0–3 each)
Up to %1$s ways to evolve. Leave the method on None to unuse a slot.
Which species use which rate is set in Personal data. The last two rates are unused by the game and equal Medium Fast
Total experience needed to be at each level. Level 1 always needs 0. Changing a level moves the later ones too unless the switch above is off
Level %1$s needs less experience than level %2$s
Rare slots: %1$s and %2$s of 100 rolls (%3$s and %4$s overall). Rolls that give nothing: %5$s of 100
18 entries. A Pokémon of level bracket b (1 to 10 is 0, 11 to 20 is 1 ...) gets entry b + slot, so neighbouring brackets share entries
11 entries, picked as entry b + (99 - roll): bracket b with a roll of 99 gets entry b, a roll of 98 entry b + 1
What each level range can give, slot 1 to 9 for common items and the two rare ones
Vertical offset of the battle sprite, and the position and size of its shadow. Offsets are signed
0 to 255, per battle sprite. A slot with no sprite (a species with one gender) cannot be edited
Left, middle and right ball in Professor Elm's lab (Chikorita, Cyndaquil and Totodile in the original)
The held item is one byte in the game, so only items 0 to 255 can be chosen.
A starter is not data in a table: it is spread over the game's code

Found by reading every script: a fixed battle, a gift or an egg. When a script puts the species in a variable first (Ho-Oh and Lugia, Latias and Latios, the Game Corner prizes, the starters), each number it can use is listed, and a change edits that number; a level that a script puts in a variable first (Ho-Oh and Lugia, one for each game version) is listed the same way (the game picks one by its version: HeartGold uses 45 for Ho-Oh and 70 for Lugia, SoulSilver the other way round). A species or a level that no script sets with a number are listed but not edited here: change the script in the Scripts editor. Roaming Pokémon are in the Roamers editor and the revived fossils in the Fossils editor; neither is a script command with a species, so they are not listed here.
A roamer's route and the way it flees depend on its species in the code, and the scripts that hide the overworld legendaries are not changed.
The scientist in the Pewter City museum asks this table which Pokémon a fossil gives. The level (20) is in his script, and the items are the ones his script and the bag know.
Wild encounters keep Cute Charm and Synchronize. A trainer's Pokémon keep their nature and gender.
Nickname and trainer name are message bank 200 (entry n and n + 13); edit them in the text editor
How fast the HP bar drains and fills in battle, from the guide "Changing the HP bar speed" (one instruction of overlay 12).
The ROM has a custom speed (shift %1$s).
Over the limit: the game reads only the first %1$s
Learned in this order as the level is reached
Apply to the %1$s shown in the list: search to narrow it. Teaching skips a species that knows the move or already has %2$s moves
%1$s left. Trade becomes a level-up; trade with an item becomes using that item.
Over the limit: the game only finds species whose header is within the first %1$s words
Only moves the parents can pass down appear here

Rows attack, columns defend. Click a cell to cycle 1x, 2x, 1/2x, 0x. The table has room for %1$s non-neutral pairs (%2$s used): setting a pair back to 1x frees a slot. Immunities of Ghost are the ones Foresight, Odd-Eye and Scrappy switch off

After a battle, a Pokémon with Pickup and no held item activates with a 1 in divisor chance, then rolls 0 to 99. The first slot whose weight is above the roll gives a common item; a roll of 98 or 99 that no weight catches gives a rare one
Part of this is not found in this ROM, so it can not be changed

Changing a ball also updates the cries table of the chooser, the seven scripts in which the rival picks the Pokémon that is strong against yours, and the species and type words in the professor's questions. Names the game shows elsewhere (the rival's lines, the Pokédex) are not touched.

The script command CreateRoamer only says which of the four starts (0 to 3); the species and level are in the game's code. Raikou and Entei take species 1 to 255, Latias a number that is a byte times a power of two (for example 380), Latios any species
A loan: the NPC lends this Pokémon and takes the same species back (vanilla Rusty, Shuckie, Kenya and Volty)
The NPC gives the first Pokémon for the second
Interactions with abilities, items and other moves; the animation flags change how the move is drawn
Super Contest condition and appeal, a Diamond, Pearl and Platinum feature
Raw; meaning depends on the item's effect
Which species can learn each one is set in the personal data editor
The clerk of the ordinary Poké Marts sells every item whose tier is at or below the player's: 0 badges is tier 1, 1 to 2 tier 2, 3 to 4 tier 3, 5 to 6 tier 4, 7 tier 5, 8 tier 6
Full: no room left for more items
Full: remove an item to add another
Search items, places or a script number…
No overworld event runs script %1$s: put it on an overworld object of a map to place the ball.
The game reserves room for %1$s spots, so a new one needs a removed one first.

Script %1$s and flag %2$s (picked up) follow from the index. Put script %3$s on an overworld object of the map to place the spot; removing or renumbering a spot leaves objects that use its script pointing at nothing.
Replace a Pokémon in every trainer party
Keeps level and everything else; changes the species only
Name and messages are in message banks 27 and 724 (messages 3n to 3n + 2); edit them in the text editor
%1$s sets this trainer picks its team from, a random few each battle. Sets are edited in the Battle Tower sets editor
Used for battle text and sprites. Class names are not editable yet
Money won = multiplier x level of the trainer's last Pokémon x a base amount
Chance that a step or cast starts an encounter
Each slot has one level and a species for morning, day and night
Pokémon cries heard when tuning the Pokégear radio
Each group has fixed slots with fixed chances: adding takes slots from the others, removing gives its slots away
Only rolled when smashing a rock does not start a wild battle (the encounter rate is set in the Wild encounters editor)
Shared by every map that uses it. Serene Grace and Super Luck move a roll one slot toward the rarer end
How the game treats this entry
The table has a fixed length of 30 towns, so towns can be changed but not added.
Where the player appears after using Fly (global position)
Where the player wakes up after losing a battle (tile position inside the map)
The place that adds the town to the Fly list (global position)
This map has no Headbutt trees, so its tables are never used. Add a tree group to give it some. The tree tile must also have the Headbutt type (6) and be blocked in the Maps editor.
Most normal trees use this table
Some normal trees use this one instead, decided by the player's Trainer ID
Trees in the special groups always use this table
%1$s. Species 0 is an empty slot; fill every slot if the map has trees
%1$s. A group is one tree, which can be headbutted from up to %2$s tiles. Coordinates are map-wide: matrix cell x 32 + tile in the map. 65535 x 65535 is unused
Which set the National Park uses: the first without the National Dex, then by the day of the week on the DS clock

The game rolls 0 to 99 and takes the first slot whose rate is at or below the roll, so rates must fall from top to bottom and end at 0. Chance = the gap to the rate above (100 for the first slot). Score is the rarity part of the judge's score
This area has no Pokémon data in the ROM.
The ten Pokémon the area gives at this time of day when no object arrangement applies
%1$s: when the player has placed the required objects (and, if set, the optional ones) in the area, this Pokémon replaces the usual ones at that time of day
Drawn red once visited, replaced by a gray block before. Positions are 8x8 tiles in the map picture
The red position is stored one tile off: the picture position is X - 1 and Y + 1. The table has a fixed length of %1$s entries.
The orange block shown when the cursor is on a town or route

The text entry is the blurb in text bank 273. A non-zero fly spot marks a town the player can fly to. What the flags do is not documented, so they are kept as they are unless you change them. The table has a fixed length of %1$s entries.
Where the player stands in the picture, as the TakePhoto script command uses it
X and Y are global positions (the whole matrix, as in the Events editor).
The icon in the Photo Album and who is next to the player
With an overworld entry of 0 the picture is a group photo of the party; otherwise it shows the player, the first Pokémon and that overworld NPC, whether or not it is on the map.
Kept as they are in the game: the constant is 0xFF01 everywhere, the parameters are used by some places and their meaning is not known
The name shown when you enter, and where the map sits in the world
Numbers are file indexes in the ROM; the matching editors open them
What the player may do on this map
The tiles of every cell, as in the Maps editor
Each cell is a map file. Click a cell to edit it; empty cells have no map.
Left click paints, right click picks. The tile type is what the game calls the tile behaviour; collision 0x80 blocks.
The map as the game draws it, without animation. Drag turns, right drag pans, Ctrl + wheel zooms, a click selects a building
Markers: blue NPC, red trainer, purple warp, green trigger, brown sign, orange building.
This map has no event file
Click a marker to select it and drag it to move it. Click the same tile again to reach events stacked on it.
3D models placed on the map. Select one here or click it in the 3D view; Move here puts the selected building where you click the ground
Rotation and scale are the raw numbers of the file (every building of the game uses 0 and 16); the 3D view does not apply them yet.
Commands as in the script command database; a jump takes a label. Flag and variable names can be used instead of numbers. Applied as you type once it is valid.
Runs when the map is entered (map change), when its screen is reset, or when the game is loaded on it.
Variable triggers (below) are listed after this point.
Run a script on map load while a variable has a value
Press play to hear what the commands play
Every script command and event that uses a flag, variable, item, trainer or overworld sprite entry

Scripts are matched by the type of the command's parameter, so a plain number that equals a variable is not told apart. Trainers on a map are found by the script number of their object (3000 + trainer - 1 or 5000 + trainer - 1).
This ROM has no readable sound archive.
Sequence %1$s, volume %2$s, file %3$s. Previews are rendered by foxhg's own player, so timbres can differ a little from the console.

Patches to the game's code and data. They change the project, not the ROM on disk: Build ROM… writes them. Each one checks the bytes it replaces first and refuses a ROM that differs from a clean HeartGold English. They were not tried in game (a patched ROM was only booted to the intro).
%1$s files in the ROM. Pick one to see its size and bytes.
Pick an overlay to see where the game loads it and its bytes.
From the overlay table (y9.bin) of the ROM
The save is kept twice (slot 0 and slot 1); the game loads the newest sound copy of each block and writes the other slot next time
What the 41 chunks of the general block are, from the game's own table (the fields inside are decoded one editor at a time)
This save has no sound general block, so there is no player to show.
This save has no sound general block, so there is no position to show.

Continue then starts on this tile, with the map's own NPCs. The map and tile must exist and be walkable: the game does not check, and a wall or a tile outside the map leaves the player where nothing works. Use a tile the player can stand on, as the ones below.
Places the game was seen to continue at:
This save has no sound general block, or its party does not read: there is no party to show.
Nickname (up to 10 characters, empty for none)
IVs 0 to 31. EVs 0 to 255 each; the game counts at most 510 in total, and only the first 252 of one stat show in its stat.
EVs total %1$s, more than the game's 510.
As stored in the save. The game shows these, so they have to agree with the level, IVs and EVs
Recalculate from the ROM's base stats
This save has no sound storage block, or its PC does not read: there are no boxes to show.
A new Pokémon needs a personality value, original trainer and met data the editor does not make yet. Move one in from the party (Party tab, Move to the PC).
A box does not keep the level or stats: the level shown is worked out from the experience, and the game recalculates the stats when the Pokémon leaves the box. The personality value is left alone.
This save has no sound general block, or its bag does not read: there is no bag to show.
Each item once, 1 to %1$s of it. The game lists them in this order.
An item the pocket already has gets the quantity added to it. The game puts an item in the pocket its item data names; one in another pocket shows there only in the editor.
This save has no sound general block, or its Pokédex does not read: there is no Pokédex to show.
%1$s seen, %2$s caught of %3$s. A species must be seen to count as caught. Forms, genders and languages are left as they are: a Pokémon marked here shows as its first gender and form.
This save has no sound general block, so there are no flags to show.

A flag or variable by number (12, or 0x6A for hex) or by part of its name. Flags are events the game remembers (a badge won, an item picked up, a door opened); variables are numbers scripts keep. Changing them can break the story: the game does not check.
Only flags that are set / variables that are not 0
%1$s is not a foxhg project folder
Drop a .nds ROM, a .sav save or a foxhg project folder, not %1$s
Could not save the settings file
Set the emulator command to use Run. Use {rom} where the ROM goes.
Choose a different file than the ROM you opened
%1$s will take %2$s's wild Pokémon, rates and levels. Your edits in those areas are replaced. Ctrl+Z undoes it.
Cannot remove the last Pokémon of %1$s
Could not add %1$s to %2$s: already there, or every Pokémon has just one slot
Doors and exits to another map header
Scripts that run when the player steps on an area
Index %1$s is already used by spot %2$s: two spots would share one script and one picked-up flag. Pick another index.
, left %1$s alone (move already there, not known, or the list is full)
Imported %1$s: the species in the file now have its moves
Move here is on: click the ground to put the selected building there
Click a building to select it
It holds %1$s items in the ARM9; more are kept in the synthetic overlay (%2$s of %3$s bytes used by all marts).
It holds up to %1$s items (%2$s now): the lists sit one after another in the ARM9. Apply the ARM9 expansion patch in the ROM toolbox to let marts grow.
It holds up to %1$s items: the mart area of the synthetic overlay is in use by something else, so marts cannot grow.
Overlay %1$s replaced; the ROM changes when it is built.
"%1$s" applied. Ctrl+Z undoes it; the ROM changes when it is built.
Open the ROM first: the party needs the level and stats, which come from its growth curves and base stats
No map uses this level script.
Installs routines in the synthetic overlay (and the ARM9 expansion if the ROM lacks it) and hooks the places that make these Pokémon. All rates start at 0.
Pokémon cry template (played with each species' own bank)
No trainer uses %1$s, so nothing would change.
No free slot for %1$s against %2$s: the table is full. Set another pair back to 1x first.
This sound has nothing to play
What the trainer says in battle. When a line shows is saved at once; a changed text is saved with Apply.
This trainer has no battle messages.
